hypotheses.reasoning: template-svc's S3 PutObject calls to s3://notifications-artifacts-prod (us-east-1) began failing at 11:07 with 503 ServiceUnavailable / reduce request rate (#92, #96, #101), and the aws-sdk retry quota ran out (#98). Because of that, template-svc returned 500 'storage write failed' to notification-svc (#89, #117), which then caused the intermittent 500s at the gateway (#93, #102, #112, #130). Before the onset, worker batch sizes and request volume were steady, so these logs don't show our own traffic spiking. S3 recovered by about 11:11:44, when renders succeeded again. There was no deploy and no config change. Redis and notif-db stayed healthy, and the gateway disk-usage warning is a red herring.
'Please reduce your request rate' could mean we exceeded our own S3 request-rate limits (a hot prefix) rather than S3 having a provider-side problem. However, there is no visible traffic increase.

verdict.recommendedAction: Check AWS Health / the S3 us-east-1 status for the 11:07–11:11 window. Add backoff and jitter to template-svc S3 writes, and consider making artifact persistence asynchronous or non-blocking for /render so an S3 hiccup doesn't fail notify requests. Also check whether key-prefix distribution could be triggering S3 SlowDown.
